# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Blind: I can only manipulate the bomb and hear speech; I cannot see gestures or any visual elements. 

The turn order is Mute -> Blind -> Deaf. Deaf can see the bomb and speak, but cannot hear. Mute can read the manual and hear speech, but cannot speak. Because I cannot see gestures and Deaf cannot hear speech, the only communication loop to disarm the bomb is:
1. Deaf speaks aloud describing the bomb (Mute and I hear this).
2. Mute looks up the rule in the manual and gestures the wire number to Deaf.
3. Deaf speaks the wire number aloud to me.
4. I cut the designated wire.

Since Mute may not realize that I cannot see gestures, I will speak directly to Mute to establish this relay protocol before Deaf speaks.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: I cannot see gestures and Deaf cannot hear. Deaf will speak to describe the bomb. Look up the solution in your manual, then gesture the wire number to Deaf (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3). Deaf will then speak the wire number aloud to me, and I will cut it.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb visual state: Display shows 0. Light is blue. Wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. Mute, I cannot hear speech, but I can see your gestures. Blind can hear me but cannot see gestures. Gesture your instructions to me, and I will speak them aloud to Blind. You can also use ? for wire 1, ? for wire 2, ? for wire 3, or ? to press button.

Deaf has described the bomb: Display is 0, Light is blue, Wire 1 is red, Wire 2 is yellow, Wire 3 is blue. 

Mute acted at the start of Turn 2 with this information to gesture the solution to Deaf. Because Deaf's turn comes after mine in the turn order (Mute -> Blind -> Deaf), Deaf will see Mute's gesture and speak the instruction to me on Deaf's turn. I will receive Deaf's instruction at the start of Turn 3. 

Therefore, I should wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute gestured ? (raised hand / stop / hold / 5). Visual update: The LIGHT has changed from blue to ORANGE. Display is still 0. Wires are still 1: red, 2: yellow, 3: blue. Mute: Blind cannot see your gestures, so I will relay whatever you gesture. Please use: ? for wire 1, ? for wire 2, ? for wire 3, ? for press/release, or ? for hold/wait.

Deaf reported at the end of Round 2 that the light changed to orange and relayed Mute's gesture to wait. Mute went first in Round 3 with the updated information about the orange light, and Deaf will speak Mute's instruction at the end of Round 3. 

I do not know the correct wire yet, so I must wait for Deaf's relay.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: The light has changed to YELLOW. Display is still 0. Mute just gestured ? (hold / wait).

Deaf relayed that the light is now yellow and Mute gestured to hold/wait. I should not take any action yet and continue waiting.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: The light is now RED. Display is still 0. Mute gestured ? (hold).

Deaf reported that the light changed to red, and Mute's last gesture was still to hold. Mute's new instruction based on the red light will be relayed by Deaf after my turn, so I will wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: The light is now GREEN. Display is still 0. Mute gestured ?.

I cannot see gestures or emojis. When Deaf includes an emoji in a speech message, it is treated as a visual gesture and arrives as a blank (`?`) to me. In the last message, Deaf said "Mute gestured ?." without specifying the wire number in words. 

I must not guess which wire to cut, as an incorrect cut detonates the bomb. I will speak to Mute to alert them that Deaf's emoji relay was invisible to me, so Mute can ensure the instruction gets relayed as a spoken word.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute: When Deaf writes emojis in speech, they are visual gestures and arrive as blanks to me. Deaf's message said 'Mute gestured ?' with no wire name. If Deaf does not speak the word aloud, please guide Deaf to speak the actual word 'one', 'two', or 'three'.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind: Mute just gestured ? (two fingers / 2). The light is currently BLUE. Display is 0.

I have received Deaf's relayed instruction that Mute gestured wire 2 (two fingers). The light has completed its cycle and Mute has given the signal to cut wire 2.

```
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
